---
title: "! applies to the result of the whole pipe, not to the first value"
ref: FUN-13
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '!c(TRUE, FALSE) |> any()'
reponse: 'FALSE'
attendu: "`TRUE`, since one of the negated values is `TRUE`"
versions: "Since R 4.1.0, which introduced |>"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
a <- c(TRUE, FALSE)
!a |> any()
quote(!a |> any())
```
:::

## Why

The `!` operator has lower precedence than `|>` and `%in%`, and even lower than comparisons. R therefore reads the whole pipe first, `a |> any()`, then negates the result: `!any(a)`, not `any(!a)`.

`quote()` shows the expression as R understood it. The same thing happens with {magrittr}'s `%>%`, and with `!x %in% y`, which means `!(x %in% y)`.

## The fix

Put the negation in parentheses, or keep it out of the pipe.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
(!a) |> any()
any(!a)
```
:::
